english_text: Tuberculosis is an infectious disease caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
sesotho_text: Tuberculosis ke bolwetse bo fetisoang bo bakoang ke bakteria ea Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

english_text: TB primarily affects the lungs but can also affect the kidneys, spine, and brain.
sesotho_text: TB haholo-holo e angoa matšoafo empa e ka boetse e angoa lipitso, mokokotlo, le boko.

english_text: TB is one of the leading infectious disease killers worldwide.
sesotho_text: TB ke e 'ngoe ea mafu a fetisoang a bolaeang batho ba bangata ka ho fetisisa lefatšeng lohle.

english_text: In 2023, approximately 10.8 million people fell ill with TB globally.
sesotho_text: Ka 2023, batho ba ka bang limilione tse 10.8 ba kulile ka TB lefatšeng lohle.

english_text: TB is both preventable and curable with the right treatment.
sesotho_text: TB e ka thibeloa le ho folisoa ka phekolo e nepahetseng.

english_text: Mycobacterium tuberculosis is a slow-growing bacterium that can remain dormant in the body for years.
sesotho_text: Mycobacterium tuberculosis ke bakteria e holang butle e ka etsang nako e telele e robetse 'meleng ka lilemo.

english_text: TB disease occurs when the immune system cannot contain the TB bacteria.
sesotho_text: Bolwetse ba TB bo etsahala ha tšireletso ea 'mele e ke ke ea laola bakteria ea TB.

english_text: South Africa has one of the highest TB burdens in the world.
sesotho_text: Afrika Boroa e na le e 'ngoe ea morwalo o moholo ka ho fetisisa oa TB lefatšeng.

english_text: TB disproportionately affects people living in poverty, overcrowded conditions, and those with weakened immune systems.
sesotho_text: TB e angoa batho ba phelang bofumeng, libakeng tse tletse batho, le ba nang le tšireletso ea 'mele e fokolang ka mokgwa o sa lekanang.

english_text: The End TB Strategy aims to reduce TB deaths by 95% and new cases by 90% by 2035.
sesotho_text: Leano la ho Felisa TB le ikemiseditse ho fokotsa lifu tsa TB ka 95% le liketsahalo tse ncha ka 90% ka 2035.

english_text: TB is classified as pulmonary TB when it affects the lungs and extrapulmonary TB when it affects other organs.
sesotho_text: TB e aroloa e le TB ea matšoafo ha e angoa matšoafo le TB ea kantle ho matšoafo ha e angoa litho tse ling.

english_text: Pulmonary TB is the most common and most infectious form of the disease.
sesotho_text: TB ea matšoafo ke mofuta o atileng ka ho fetisisa le o fetisoang ka ho fetisisa oa bolwetse.

english_text: Extrapulmonary TB can affect the lymph nodes, pleura, bones, joints, and central nervous system.
sesotho_text: TB ea kantle ho matšoafo e ka angoa li-lymph node, pleura, masapo, maqhoa, le tsamaiso ea bohareng ea methapo.

english_text: Miliary TB is a severe form of the disease where bacteria spread through the bloodstream to multiple organs.
sesotho_text: TB ea miliary ke mofuta o matla oa bolwetse moo bakteria e phatlalatsang ka mali ho ea litho tse ngata.

english_text: TB meningitis is a life-threatening form of extrapulmonary TB affecting the brain and spinal cord.
sesotho_text: TB meningitis ke mofuta oa TB ea kantle ho matšoafo o kotsi ea bophelo o angoa boko le mokokotlo.

english_text: Spinal TB, also known as Pott's disease, can cause vertebral destruction and paralysis if untreated.
sesotho_text: TB ea mokokotlo, e tsebahala hape e le bolwetse ba Pott, e ka baka ho senyeha ha masapo a mokokotlo le ho fofotsoa haeba e sa phekoluoe.

english_text: TB of the lymph nodes, called scrofula, presents as painless swelling in the neck.
sesotho_text: TB ea li-lymph node, e bitsoa scrofula, e bontšoa e le ho ruruha ho sa bohlokong molaleng.

english_text: TB pericarditis involves infection of the sac surrounding the heart and can be fatal.
sesotho_text: TB pericarditis e kenyelletsa tšoaetso ea saka e potileng pelo mme e ka bolaea.

english_text: Abdominal TB can affect the intestines, peritoneum, and abdominal lymph nodes.
sesotho_text: TB ea mpa e ka angoa mala, peritoneum, le li-lymph node tsa mpa.

english_text: TB of the urinary tract can cause blood in the urine and kidney damage.
sesotho_text: TB ea tsela ea moroto e ka baka mali morotong le kotsi ea lipitso.

english_text: TB spreads through the air when a person with active pulmonary TB coughs, sneezes, or speaks.
sesotho_text: TB e phatlalala ka moea ha motho ea nang le TB ea matšoafo e sebetsang a kohoa, a thimola, kapa a bua.

english_text: TB is not spread by touching, sharing food, or kissing.
sesotho_text: TB ha e phatlalatsoe ka ho ama, ho arolelana lijo, kapa ho atana.

english_text: A single cough from a person with active TB can release thousands of infectious droplet nuclei.
sesotho_text: Ho kohoa ha motho ea nang le TB e sebetsang ka nako e le ngoe ho ka lokolla lintlha tse likete tsa metsi a fetisoang.

english_text: TB bacteria can remain suspended in the air for several hours in poorly ventilated spaces.
sesotho_text: Bakteria ea TB e ka lula e phaphame moeeng ka maho a mang libakeng tse se nang moea o lekaneng.

english_text: Close and prolonged contact with an infectious TB patient increases the risk of transmission.
sesotho_text: Ho kopana haufi le nako e telele le mokuloi ea nang le TB e fetisoang ho eketsa kotsi ea phetisetso.

english_text: Household contacts of TB patients are at highest risk of infection.
sesotho_text: Batho ba kopanang le bakuli ba TB malapa ba leng kotsing e phahameng ka ho fetisisa ea tšoaetso.

english_text: Healthcare workers are at elevated risk of TB due to occupational exposure.
sesotho_text: Basebetsi ba bophelo bo botle ba leng kotsing e phahameng ea TB ka lebaka la ho hlahisoa mosebetsing.

english_text: Good ventilation in homes, clinics, and public spaces reduces TB transmission risk.
sesotho_text: Moea o motle malapeng, likhlinikhing, le libakeng tsa sechaba o fokotsa kotsi ea phetisetso ea TB.

english_text: Ultraviolet germicidal irradiation (UVGI) can kill TB bacteria in the air of high-risk settings.
sesotho_text: Ho phahamisoa ha UVGI ho ka bolaea bakteria ea TB moeeng libakeng tse leng kotsing e phahameng.

english_text: N95 respirators protect healthcare workers from inhaling TB droplet nuclei.
sesotho_text: Li-respirator tsa N95 li sireletsa basebetsi ba bophelo bo botle ho hema lintlha tsa metsi a TB.

english_text: Surgical masks worn by TB patients reduce the number of infectious particles released into the air.
sesotho_text: Li-mask tsa opereishene tse aperoang ke bakuli ba TB li fokotsa palo ea likaroloana tse fetisoang tse lokollwang moeeng.

english_text: People with latent TB infection are not infectious and cannot spread TB to others.
sesotho_text: Batho ba nang le tšoaetso ea TB e patileng ha ba fetiseloe mme ha ba khone ho phatlalatsela TB ho ba bang.

english_text: Only people with active pulmonary TB disease can transmit the infection.
sesotho_text: Batho ba nang le bolwetse ba TB ea matšoafo e sebetsang feela ba ka fetisetsa tšoaetso.

english_text: TB transmission is more likely in crowded settings such as prisons, mines, and informal settlements.
sesotho_text: Phetisetso ea TB e atile haholo libakeng tse tletse batho joalo ka likotsofatso, merafo, le metse e sa reriloeng.

english_text: Mineworkers are at particularly high risk of TB due to silica dust exposure and crowded living conditions.
sesotho_text: Basebetsi ba merafo ba leng kotsing e phahameng haholo ea TB ka lebaka la ho hlahisoa lerole la silica le maemo a bophelo a tletse batho.

english_text: Silicosis caused by silica dust exposure greatly increases the risk of developing TB.
sesotho_text: Silicosis e bakoang ke ho hlahisoa lerole la silica e eketsa haholo kotsi ea ho ba le TB.

english_text: TB transmission in schools can occur when a teacher or student has undiagnosed active TB.
sesotho_text: Phetisetso ea TB likolong e ka etsahala ha mosuoe kapa moithuti a na le TB e sebetsang e sa fumanoe.

english_text: Air travel can facilitate TB transmission in confined aircraft cabins during long flights.
sesotho_text: Ho tsamaea ka sefofane ho ka khothaletsa phetisetso ea TB ka hare ho likamore tse koalehileng tsa sefofane nakong ea lieto tse telele.

english_text: Contact tracing is essential to identify and test people who may have been exposed to TB.
sesotho_text: Ho latela bakopani ho bohlokoa ho tseba le ho lekoa batho ba ka bang ba hlahisitsoe TB.

english_text: TB transmission can be interrupted by early diagnosis and prompt initiation of effective treatment.
sesotho_text: Phetisetso ea TB e ka emisoa ka ho fumanoa kapele le ho qala phekolo e sebetsang hang hang.

english_text: The most common symptom of pulmonary TB is a persistent cough lasting more than two weeks.
sesotho_text: Letšoao le atileng ka ho fetisisa la TB ea matšoafo ke ho kohoa ho tsoelang pele ho feta libeke tse peli.

english_text: TB symptoms include coughing up blood or blood-stained sputum.
sesotho_text: Matšoao a TB a kenyelletsa ho kohoa mali kapa mathe a nang le mali.

english_text: Night sweats are a classic symptom of active TB disease.
sesotho_text: Molapo oa bosiu ke letšoao la kamehla la bolwetse ba TB bo sebetsang.

english_text: Unexplained weight loss is a common symptom of TB and other serious illnesses.
sesotho_text: Ho lahleheloa ke boima ho sa hlalositsoeng ke letšoao le tloaelehileng la TB le mafu a mang a matla.

english_text: Fever, fatigue, and loss of appetite are general symptoms associated with active TB.
sesotho_text: Feberu, ho lapala, le ho lahleheloa ke takatso ea lijo ke matšoao a kakaretso a amanang le TB e sebetsang.

english_text: Chest pain and difficulty breathing can occur in TB patients with pleural involvement.
sesotho_text: Mahloko a sefubeng le bothata ba ho hema li ka etsahala ho bakuli ba TB ba nang le bothata ba pleura.

english_text: TB symptoms can be mild at first and worsen gradually over weeks or months.
sesotho_text: Matšoao a TB a ka ba bonolo qalong mme a mpe butle butle ka libeke kapa likhoeli.

english_text: Children with TB may present with failure to thrive, poor weight gain, and persistent fever.
sesotho_text: Bana ba nang le TB ba ka bontša ho hloleha ho hola, ho eketseha ha boima ho fokolang, le feberu e tsoelang pele.

english_text: Swollen lymph nodes in the neck or armpits may indicate extrapulmonary TB.
sesotho_text: Li-lymph node tse ruruhetse molaleng kapa likhokoaneng li ka bontša TB ea kantle ho matšoafo.

english_text: Back pain and stiffness can be symptoms of spinal TB.
sesotho_text: Mahloko a mokokotlo le ho thatafala li ka ba matšoao a TB ea mokokotlo.

english_text: Headache, confusion, and neck stiffness are warning signs of TB meningitis.
sesotho_text: Mahloko a hlooho, ho tsieleha, le ho thatafala ha molala ke lišoaetso tsa tlhokahalo ea TB meningitis.

english_text: Abdominal pain and swelling may indicate abdominal TB.
sesotho_text: Mahloko a mpa le ho ruruha li ka bontša TB ea mpa.

english_text: Haematuria — blood in the urine — can be a sign of urinary tract TB.
sesotho_text: Haematuria — mali morotong — e ka ba letšoao la TB ea tsela ea moroto.

english_text: Joint pain and swelling may indicate TB arthritis, especially in the hip or knee.
sesotho_text: Mahloko a maqhoa le ho ruruha li ka bontša TB arthritis, haholo-holo serope kapa leqhoa.

english_text: Many people with TB delay seeking care because early symptoms resemble a common cold or flu.
sesotho_text: Batho ba bangata ba nang le TB ba lieha ho batla tlhokomelo hobane matšoao a pele a tšoana le mofetše kapa flu.

english_text: Anyone with a cough lasting more than two weeks should be evaluated for TB.
sesotho_text: Motho ofe kapa ofe ea nang le ho kohoa ho feta libeke tse peli o lokela ho hlahlobeloa TB.

english_text: TB symptoms in HIV-positive patients may be atypical and harder to recognise.
sesotho_text: Matšoao a TB ho bakuli ba nang le HIV a ka ba a sa tloaelehang mme a thata ho tseba.

english_text: Elderly patients with TB may present with fewer classic symptoms, making diagnosis more challenging.
sesotho_text: Bakuli ba baholo ba nang le TB ba ka bontša matšoao a manyenyane a kamehla, e leng ntho e etsang hore ho fumana bolwetse ho be thata haholo.

english_text: Diabetic patients with TB may have more severe disease and atypical presentations.
sesotho_text: Bakuli ba nang le tsoekere le TB ba ka ba le bolwetse bo matla haholo le ho bontšoa ha bolwetse ho sa tloaelehang.

english_text: If you have any symptoms of TB, visit your nearest clinic as soon as possible for testing.
sesotho_text: Haeba u na le matšoao afe kafe a TB, etela kliniki ea hau e haufi kamoo ho khonehang ka potlako bakeng sa liteko.

english_text: TB diagnosis is confirmed by detecting Mycobacterium tuberculosis in sputum or other clinical specimens.
sesotho_text: Tlhahlobo ea TB e netefatsoa ka ho fumana Mycobacterium tuberculosis mathe kapa lisampole tse ling tsa kliniki.

english_text: Sputum smear microscopy is a rapid, low-cost test used to detect TB bacteria in sputum.
sesotho_text: Microscopy ea ho hlakola mathe ke tlhahlobo ea potlako, e tlase litefisong, e sebelisoa ho fumana bakteria ea TB mathe.

english_text: GeneXpert MTB/RIF is a rapid molecular test that detects TB and rifampicin resistance within two hours.
sesotho_text: GeneXpert MTB/RIF ke tlhahlobo ea molecular ea potlako e fumanang TB le khakanyo ea rifampicin ka hare ho maho a mabeli.

english_text: GeneXpert is now the recommended initial diagnostic test for TB in most high-burden countries.
sesotho_text: GeneXpert joale ke tlhahlobo ea pele ea ho fumana bolwetse e khothalletsoa bakeng sa TB linaheng tse ngata tse nang le morwalo o moholo.

english_text: Sputum culture remains the gold standard for TB diagnosis and drug susceptibility testing.
sesotho_text: Culture ea mathe e ntse e le sesupo sa tšimong ea ho fumana TB le ho lekoa ha ho amehela ha meriana.

english_text: TB culture can take 2 to 8 weeks to produce results due to the slow growth of Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
sesotho_text: Culture ea TB e ka nka libeke tse 2 ho isa ho tse 8 ho hlahisa liphetho ka lebaka la ho hola butle ha Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

english_text: Chest X-ray is used to support TB diagnosis by identifying lung abnormalities.
sesotho_text: X-ray ea sefuba e sebelisoa ho tshehetsa tlhahlobo ea TB ka ho tseba ho sa tloaelehang ha matšoafo.

english_text: Chest X-ray findings in TB include upper lobe infiltrates, cavities, and hilar lymphadenopathy.
sesotho_text: Liphetho tsa X-ray ea sefuba ho TB li kenyelletsa ho kenella ha karolo e holimo ea matšoafo, likhoba, le ho ruruha ha li-lymph node tsa hilar.

english_text: A normal chest X-ray does not rule out TB, especially in HIV-positive patients.
sesotho_text: X-ray ea sefuba e tloaelehileng ha e felise TB, haholo-holo ho bakuli ba nang le HIV.

english_text: The tuberculin skin test (TST) detects immune sensitisation to TB antigens but cannot distinguish latent from active TB.
sesotho_text: Tlhahlobo ea letlalo ea tuberculin (TST) e fumana ho amehela ha tšireletso ea 'mele ho li-antigen tsa TB empa e ke ke ea arola TB e patileng le e sebetsang.

english_text: Interferon-gamma release assays (IGRAs) are blood tests used to diagnose latent TB infection.
sesotho_text: Li-assay tsa ho lokolla interferon-gamma (IGRAs) ke liteko tsa mali tse sebelisoa ho fumana tšoaetso ea TB e patileng.

english_text: IGRAs are preferred over TST in people who have received the BCG vaccine.
sesotho_text: IGRAs li khahloa ho feta TST ho batho ba fumaneng ente ea BCG.

english_text: Drug susceptibility testing (DST) determines which antibiotics will be effective against a patient's TB strain.
sesotho_text: Ho lekoa ha ho amehela ha meriana (DST) ho bua hore na li-antibiotic life li tla sebetsa khahlanong le mofuta oa TB oa mokuloi.

english_text: Line probe assays (LPA) can rapidly detect resistance to first and second-line TB drugs.
sesotho_text: Li-assay tsa line probe (LPA) li ka fumana kapele khakanyo ea meriana ea TB ea mola oa pele le oa bobeli.

english_text: Whole genome sequencing (WGS) is an advanced tool for detecting drug resistance and TB strain typing.
sesotho_text: Ho latelana ha genome yohle (WGS) ke sesebelisoa se tsoetseng pele sa ho fumana khakanyo ea meriana le ho bua mefuta ea TB.

english_text: Bronchoscopy may be used to collect specimens for TB diagnosis when sputum tests are negative.
sesotho_text: Bronchoscopy e ka sebelisoa ho kgotha lisampole bakeng sa tlhahlobo ea TB ha liteko tsa mathe li senyenyane.

english_text: Fine needle aspiration biopsy is used to diagnose TB lymphadenitis.
sesotho_text: Biopsy ea ho hula ka mosipi o monyenyane e sebelisoa ho fumana TB lymphadenitis.

english_text: Lumbar puncture is performed to diagnose TB meningitis by examining cerebrospinal fluid.
sesotho_text: Ho toboa mokokotlo ho etsoa ho fumana TB meningitis ka ho hlahloba metsi a boko le mokokotlo.

english_text: Urine lipoarabinomannan (LAM) testing is a rapid bedside test for TB in HIV-positive patients with low CD4 counts.
sesotho_text: Ho lekoa ha lipoarabinomannan (LAM) ea moroto ke tlhahlobo ea potlako ea bokamoso bakeng sa TB ho bakuli ba nang le HIV ba nang le palo e tlase ea CD4.

english_text: TB diagnosis in children is challenging because children often cannot produce sputum for testing.
sesotho_text: Ho fumana TB ho bana ho thata hobane bana hangata ha ba khone ho hlahisa mathe bakeng sa liteko.

english_text: Gastric aspirate specimens can be used to diagnose TB in young children who cannot expectorate sputum.
sesotho_text: Lisampole tsa ho hula mpa li ka sebelisoa ho fumana TB ho bana ba banyenyane ba ke ke ba hlahisa mathe.

english_text: Stool-based GeneXpert testing is an emerging non-invasive method for diagnosing TB in children.
sesotho_text: Ho lekoa ha GeneXpert ho thehiloeng holim'a manyolo ke mokoa o sa keneng ka hare o hlahang oa ho fumana TB ho bana.

english_text: Screening for TB should be offered to all HIV-positive patients at every clinical encounter.
sesotho_text: Ho hlahlobeloa ha TB ho lokela ho fanoa ho bakuli bohle ba nang le HIV letsetsong le leng le le leng la kliniki.

english_text: The WHO four-symptom screen — cough, fever, weight loss, night sweats — is used to identify TB suspects.
sesotho_text: Tlhahlobo ea matšoao a mane a WHO — ho kohoa, feberu, ho lahleheloa ke boima, molapo oa bosiu — e sebelisoa ho tseba ba nahanoa ba nang le TB.

english_text: Point-of-care TB diagnostics improve access to testing in remote and resource-limited settings.
sesotho_text: Litlhahlobo tsa TB tsa sebaka sa tlhokomelo li ntlafatsa phihlello ea liteko libakeng tse hole le tse hlokang mehloli.

english_text: Delayed TB diagnosis leads to continued transmission and worse patient outcomes.
sesotho_text: Ho lieha ha tlhahlobo ea TB ho lebisa ho tsoela pele ha phetisetso le liphetho tse mpe tsa bakuli.

english_text: TB diagnosis requires a combination of clinical assessment, laboratory tests, and imaging.
sesotho_text: Tlhahlobo ea TB e hloka kopano ea tlhahlobo ea kliniki, liteko tsa laboratori, le ho nka lifoto.

english_text: All TB patients should be tested for HIV at the time of TB diagnosis.
sesotho_text: Bakuli bohle ba TB ba lokela ho hlahlobeloa HIV nako ea tlhahlobo ea TB.

english_text: TB notification to public health authorities is mandatory in most countries to enable contact tracing.
sesotho_text: Ho tsebisa TB mabusetong a bophelo bo botle ba sechaba ho hlokeha linaheng tse ngata ho khothaletsa ho latela bacopani.

english_text: Digital chest X-ray with AI-assisted reading is improving TB screening capacity in high-burden settings.
sesotho_text: X-ray ea sefuba ea dijithale e nang le ho bala ho tshehetsoang ke AI e ntlafatsa bokgoni ba ho hlahlobeloa ha TB libakeng tse nang le morwalo o moholo.

english_text: I coughed for three months before I went to the clinic — I did not know it could be TB.
sesotho_text: Ke kohile ka likhoeli tse tharo pele ke ea klinikhing — ha ke a tseba hore e ka ba TB.

english_text: The nurse took my sputum sample and told me I would have results in two hours.
sesotho_text: Mooki o nkile sampole ea mathe a ka mme a mpolela hore ke tla ba le liphetho ka hare ho maho a mabeli.

english_text: When the doctor told me I had TB, I was scared because I thought it was a death sentence.
sesotho_text: Ha ngaka e mpolela hore ke na le TB, ke ne ke tšaba hobane ke nahana hore ke kahlolo ea lefu.

english_text: I was relieved to finally have a diagnosis after months of feeling unwell.
sesotho_text: Ke khotsofetse ho fumana tlhahlobo qetellong ka mor'a likhoeli tsa ho ikutloa ke sa phela hantle.

english_text: The clinic tested me for both TB and HIV on the same day.
sesotho_text: Kliniki e nhlahlobelitse TB le HIV letsatsi le leng.

english_text: My child was diagnosed with TB after I was found to have the disease.
sesotho_text: Ngoana oa ka o fumanoe a na le TB ka mor'a hore nna ke fumanoe ke na le bolwetse.

english_text: I was embarrassed to tell my family I had TB because of the stigma in our community.
sesotho_text: Ke ne ke hlajoa ke maswabi ho bolella lelapa la ka hore ke na le TB ka lebaka la kekello sechabeng sa rona.

english_text: The X-ray showed shadows on my lungs and the doctor explained what that meant.
sesotho_text: X-ray e bontšitse mehloli matšoafong a ka mme ngaka e hlalosa hore na seo se bolela eng.

english_text: I had to give three sputum samples over two days before the diagnosis was confirmed.
sesotho_text: Ke ne ke hloka ho fana ka lisampole tse tharo tsa mathe ka matsatsi a mabeli pele tlhahlobo e netefatsoa.

english_text: Nobody in my family had ever had TB before, so we did not recognise the symptoms.
sesotho_text: Ha ho motho lelapa la ka a neng a na le TB pele, kahoo ha re a tseba matšoao.

english_text: Active case finding involves proactively screening high-risk populations for TB outside of health facilities.
sesotho_text: Ho batla liketsahalo tse sebetsang ho kenyelletsa ho hlahlobeloa ha sechaba se leng kotsing e phahameng bakeng sa TB kantle ho likamore tsa bophelo bo botle.

english_text: Mass TB screening campaigns in high-burden communities can identify undiagnosed cases.
sesotho_text: Mananeo a ho hlahlobeloa ha TB ka bongata sechabeng se nang le morwalo o moholo a ka tseba liketsahalo tse sa fumanoe.

english_text: TB screening should be integrated into routine health services including antenatal care and HIV clinics.
sesotho_text: Ho hlahlobeloa ha TB ho lokela ho kopanyoa le litshebeletso tsa kamehla tsa bophelo bo botle ho kenyelletsa tlhokomelo pele ho tsoalo le likhliniki tsa HIV.

english_text: Community health workers play a vital role in TB case finding and patient support.
sesotho_text: Basebetsi ba bophelo bo botle ba sechaba ba bua karolo ea bohlokoa ho fumana liketsahalo tsa TB le tshehetso ea bakuli.

english_text: Mobile TB testing units can bring diagnostic services to remote and underserved communities.
sesotho_text: Liqenehelo tsa liteko tsa TB tse tsamaelang li ka tlisa litshebeletso tsa tlhahlobo sechabeng se hole le se sa sebelisoeng hantle.

english_text: Workplace TB screening programmes are important in high-risk industries such as mining.
sesotho_text: Mananeo a ho hlahlobeloa ha TB mafapheng a mosebetsi a bohlokoa meahong e leng kotsing e phahameng joalo ka merafo.

english_text: School-based TB screening can identify children with undiagnosed TB and latent infection.
sesotho_text: Ho hlahlobeloa ha TB ho thehiloeng sekolong ho ka tseba bana ba nang le TB e sa fumanoe le tšoaetso e patileng.

english_text: Prison TB screening on entry and exit is essential to prevent TB spread in correctional facilities.
sesotho_text: Ho hlahlobeloa ha TB likotsofatsong ha ho kenoa le ha ho tsoa ho bohlokoa ho thibela phatlalalo ea TB likamoreng tsa ho loka.

english_text: TB screening of refugees and migrants at border crossings can prevent cross-border transmission.
sesotho_text: Ho hlahlobeloa ha TB ha baphaphathehi le baahi ba fetang meeling ea linaha ho ka thibela phetisetso ea meeling.

english_text: Regular TB screening of healthcare workers protects both staff and patients.
sesotho_text: Ho hlahlobeloa ha TB ha kamehla ha basebetsi ba bophelo bo botle ho sireletsa basebetsi le bakuli.

english_text: The highest TB burdens are found in South-East Asia, Africa, and the Western Pacific regions.
sesotho_text: Morwalo o moholo ka ho fetisisa oa TB o fumanoa Asia Boroa-bochabela, Afrika, le libakeng tsa Pacific Bophirima.

english_text: India, Indonesia, China, the Philippines, and Pakistan account for more than half of global TB cases.
sesotho_text: India, Indonesia, China, Philippines, le Pakistan li bua karolo e fetang halofo ea liketsahalo tsa TB lefatšeng lohle.

english_text: TB incidence has been declining globally but the rate of decline is too slow to meet End TB targets.
sesotho_text: Palo ea litšoaetso tse ncha tsa TB e theohile lefatšeng lohle empa lebelo la ho theohela le lieha haholo ho fihlela lipheo tsa ho Felisa TB.

english_text: Men are more likely to develop active TB than women, but women face greater social consequences.
sesotho_text: Banna ba na le monyetla o moholo oa ho ba le TB e sebetsang ho feta basali, empa basali ba tobana le litlamorao tse kholo tsa sechaba.

english_text: Children under five years of age are at high risk of severe and disseminated TB disease.
sesotho_text: Bana ba tlase ho lilemo tse hlano ba leng kotsing e phahameng ea bolwetse ba TB bo matla le bo phatlalalaneng.

english_text: Older adults are at increased risk of TB reactivation due to waning immunity.
sesotho_text: Batho ba baholo ba leng kotsing e eketsehileng ea ho vuseletsa ha TB ka lebaka la ho fokotsehela ha tšireletso ea 'mele.

english_text: TB mortality has been declining globally but TB remains a major killer, especially among HIV-positive people.
sesotho_text: Lefu la TB le theohile lefatšeng lohle empa TB e ntse e bolaea batho ba bangata, haholo-holo ho batho ba nang le HIV.

english_text: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted TB services and led to an increase in TB deaths between 2020 and 2022.
sesotho_text: Lefu la COVID-19 le phephetse litshebeletso tsa TB mme la lebisa ho eketseheng ha lifu tsa TB pakeng tsa 2020 le 2022.

english_text: Undernutrition is the single largest risk factor for TB globally.
sesotho_text: Ho hloka phepo ke ntlha e le 'ngoe e kholo ka ho fetisisa ea kotsi ea TB lefatšeng lohle.

english_text: Diabetes mellitus triples the risk of developing active TB disease.
sesotho_text: Tsoekere e katisa kotsi ea ho ba le bolwetse ba TB bo sebetsang ka makhetlo a mararo.

english_text: HIV infection is the strongest known risk factor for progression from latent TB to active TB disease.
sesotho_text: Tšoaetso ea HIV ke ntlha e tsebahetseng e matla ka ho fetisisa ea kotsi ea ho tsoela pele ho tsoa TB e patileng ho ea ho TB e sebetsang.

english_text: Smoking increases the risk of TB infection, active disease, and death.
sesotho_text: Ho tsuba ho eketsa kotsi ea tšoaetso ea TB, bolwetse bo sebetsang, le lefu.

english_text: Alcohol use disorder is associated with increased TB risk and poor treatment outcomes.
sesotho_text: Bolwetse ba tšebediso ea joala bo amahanngoa le kotsi e eketsehileng ea TB le liphetho tse mpe tsa phekolo.

english_text: Immunosuppressive therapy, including corticosteroids and TNF-alpha inhibitors, increases TB risk.
sesotho_text: Phekolo ea ho laola tšireletso ea 'mele, ho kenyelletsa li-corticosteroid le li-inhibitor tsa TNF-alpha, e eketsa kotsi ea TB.

english_text: Chronic kidney disease patients have a significantly elevated risk of developing active TB.
sesotho_text: Bakuli ba nang le bolwetse ba lipitso ba nako e telele ba na le kotsi e phahameng haholo ea ho ba le TB e sebetsang.

english_text: Organ transplant recipients are at high risk of TB due to long-term immunosuppression.
sesotho_text: Batho ba fumanang litho tse fetisitsoeng ba leng kotsing e phahameng ea TB ka lebaka la ho laoloa ha tšireletso ea 'mele nako e telele.

english_text: People who have been previously treated for TB are at risk of relapse or reinfection.
sesotho_text: Batho ba neng ba phekoluoa TB pele ba leng kotsing ea ho khutlela morao kapa ho tšoaetsoa hape.

english_text: Overcrowded housing increases TB transmission risk within households and communities.
sesotho_text: Malapa a tletse batho a eketsa kotsi ea phetisetso ea TB malapa le sechabeng.

english_text: Homelessness is associated with high TB prevalence due to overcrowding, poor nutrition, and limited healthcare access.
sesotho_text: Ho hloka ntlo ho amahanngoa le palo e phahameng ea TB ka lebaka la ho tletse batho, phepo e fokolang, le phihlello e fokolang ea tlhokomelo ea bophelo bo botle.

english_text: Incarcerated individuals have TB rates many times higher than the general population.
sesotho_text: Batho ba khotsofatsoang ba na le likhato tsa TB tse phahameng makhetlo a mangata ho feta sechaba ka kakaretso.

english_text: After inhalation, TB bacteria are engulfed by alveolar macrophages in the lungs.
sesotho_text: Ka mor'a ho hema, bakteria ea TB e metsooa ke li-macrophage tsa alveolar matšoafong.

english_text: The immune system forms granulomas to contain TB bacteria, preventing active disease in most people.
sesotho_text: Tšireletso ea 'mele e theha li-granuloma ho laola bakteria ea TB, e thibela bolwetse bo sebetsang ho batho ba bangata.

english_text: In latent TB infection, bacteria remain alive but dormant inside granulomas.
sesotho_text: Ho tšoaetsoa ha TB e patileng, bakteria e ntse e phela empa e robetse ka hare ho li-granuloma.

english_text: Reactivation of latent TB occurs when the immune system weakens and can no longer contain the bacteria.
sesotho_text: Ho vuseletsa ha TB e patileng ho etsahala ha tšireletso ea 'mele e fokotsehela mme e ke ke ea ntse e laola bakteria.

english_text: Cavitation in the lungs occurs when TB destroys lung tissue, creating air-filled spaces visible on X-ray.
sesotho_text: Ho etsahala ha likhoba matšoafong ho etsahala ha TB e senya lisele tsa matšoafo, e theha libaka tse tletse moea tse bonahalang ho X-ray.

english_text: Cavitary TB lesions contain large numbers of bacteria and are highly infectious.
sesotho_text: Maqeba a TB a nang le likhoba a na le palo e kholo ea bakteria mme a fetiseloa haholo.

english_text: Haemoptysis — coughing up blood — results from erosion of blood vessels by TB bacteria in the lungs.
sesotho_text: Haemoptysis — ho kohoa mali — e hlaha ho tsoa ho ho senyeha ha methapo ea mali ke bakteria ea TB matšoafong.

english_text: Pleural effusion in TB occurs when bacteria or immune products irritate the pleural lining of the lungs.
sesotho_text: Ho tšoaetsa ha pleural ho TB ho etsahala ha bakteria kapa lihlahisoa tsa tšireletso ea 'mele li khathatsa letlalo la pleural la matšoafo.

english_text: TB bacteria can spread through the lymphatic system to distant organs.
sesotho_text: Bakteria ea TB e ka phatlalala ka tsamaiso ea lymphatic ho ea litho tse hole.

english_text: Haematogenous spread of TB bacteria leads to miliary TB, with tiny lesions throughout the body.
sesotho_text: Phatlalalo ea bakteria ea TB ka mali e lebisa ho TB ea miliary, e nang le maqeba a manyenyane 'meleng ka bophara.

english_text: TB is treated with a combination of antibiotics taken over several months.
sesotho_text: TB e phekoluoa ka kopano ea li-antibiotic tse nkuoang ka likhoeli tse ngata.

english_text: Standard first-line TB treatment consists of four drugs: isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol.
sesotho_text: Phekolo ea kamehla ea mola oa pele ea TB e bopiloe ke meriana e mene: isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, le ethambutol.

english_text: The standard TB treatment regimen for drug-sensitive TB lasts six months.
sesotho_text: Leano la phekolo la kamehla la TB bakeng sa TB e amehang ke meriana le nka likhoeli tse tšeletseng.

english_text: The intensive phase of TB treatment lasts two months and uses four drugs.
sesotho_text: Nako ea matla ea phekolo ea TB e nka likhoeli tse peli mme e sebelisa meriana e mene.

english_text: The continuation phase of TB treatment lasts four months and uses two drugs: isoniazid and rifampicin.
sesotho_text: Nako ea ho tsoela pele ea phekolo ea TB e nka likhoeli tse nne mme e sebelisa meriana e mebeli: isoniazid le rifampicin.

english_text: TB treatment must be completed in full even if symptoms improve before the end of treatment.
sesotho_text: Phekolo ea TB e lokela ho phethoa ka botlalo le haeba matšoao a ntlafala pele ho qetela ha phekolo.

english_text: Stopping TB treatment early can lead to treatment failure and drug resistance.
sesotho_text: Ho emisa phekolo ea TB kapele ho ka lebisa ho hloleha ha phekolo le khakanyo ea meriana.

english_text: Fixed-dose combination (FDC) tablets simplify TB treatment by combining multiple drugs in one pill.
sesotho_text: Lipilisi tsa kopano ea dose e tsitsitseng (FDC) li bonofatsa phekolo ea TB ka ho kopanya meriana e mengata pilisini e le ngoe.

english_text: FDC tablets reduce the pill burden and improve adherence in TB patients.
sesotho_text: Lipilisi tsa FDC li fokotsa morwalo oa lipilisi le ho ntlafatsa ho latela ho bakuli ba TB.

english_text: All TB patients should receive directly observed treatment (DOT) or an equivalent adherence support strategy.
sesotho_text: Bakuli bohle ba TB ba lokela ho fumana phekolo e shebilloeng ka kotloloho (DOT) kapa leano le lekanang la tshehetso ea ho latela.

english_text: Directly observed treatment involves a healthcare worker or trained supporter watching the patient take each dose.
sesotho_text: Phekolo e shebilloeng ka kotloloho e kenyelletsa mosebetsi oa bophelo bo botle kapa motshehetsi o koetlisitsoeng ho sheba mokuloi ha a nka dose le 'ngoe le e 'ngoe.

english_text: Video-observed therapy (VOT) allows patients to take their TB medication while being observed via a smartphone.
sesotho_text: Phekolo e shebilloeng ka video (VOT) e lumella bakuli ho nka meriana ea TB ha ba shebiloe ka smartphone.

english_text: TB treatment should be started as soon as the diagnosis is confirmed.
sesotho_text: Phekolo ea TB e lokela ho qaloa hang hang ha tlhahlobo e netefatsoa.

english_text: A shorter four-month TB treatment regimen has been approved for non-severe TB in children.
sesotho_text: Leano la phekolo ea TB la likhoeli tse nne le khutšoanyane le amohetsoe bakeng sa TB e sa matla ho bana.

english_text: Nutritional support should be provided alongside TB treatment to improve outcomes.
sesotho_text: Tshehetso ea phepo e lokela ho fanoa hammoho le phekolo ea TB ho ntlafatsa liphetho.

english_text: Isoniazid inhibits mycolic acid synthesis in the TB bacterial cell wall.
sesotho_text: Isoniazid e thibela tlhahiso ea mycolic acid leboteng la lisele tsa bakteria ea TB.

english_text: Rifampicin inhibits bacterial RNA polymerase and is the most important drug in TB treatment.
sesotho_text: Rifampicin e thibela RNA polymerase ea bakteria mme ke moriana o bohlokoa ka ho fetisisa ho phekolo ea TB.

english_text: Pyrazinamide is active against TB bacteria in acidic environments such as inside macrophages.
sesotho_text: Pyrazinamide e sebetsa khahlanong le bakteria ea TB tikolohong ea asiti joalo ka ka hare ho li-macrophage.

english_text: Ethambutol inhibits the synthesis of the TB bacterial cell wall and is used to prevent resistance.
sesotho_text: Ethambutol e thibela tlhahiso ea lebota la lisele tsa bakteria ea TB mme e sebelisoa ho thibela khakanyo.

english_text: Pyridoxine (vitamin B6) is given alongside isoniazid to prevent peripheral neuropathy.
sesotho_text: Pyridoxine (vitamin B6) e fanoa hammoho le isoniazid ho thibela neuropathy ea maphethelo.

english_text: Rifampicin is a potent inducer of liver enzymes and can reduce the effectiveness of many other medications.
sesotho_text: Rifampicin ke moqhosi o matla oa li-enzyme tsa sebete mme e ka fokotsa bokgoni ba meriana e mengata e meng.

english_text: Rifampicin turns urine, sweat, and tears orange — patients should be warned about this harmless side effect.
sesotho_text: Rifampicin e fetola moroto, molapo, le meokho e be orange — bakuli ba lokela ho lemosoa ka tlhamorao ena e sa kotsi.

english_text: Isoniazid can cause drug-induced liver injury; liver function should be monitored during treatment.
sesotho_text: Isoniazid e ka baka kotsi ea sebete e bakoang ke moriana; tšebetso ea sebete e lokela ho hlahlojoa nakong ea phekolo.

english_text: Pyrazinamide is the most hepatotoxic of the first-line TB drugs.
sesotho_text: Pyrazinamide ke e kotsi ka ho fetisisa ho sebete ho meriana ea mola oa pele ea TB.

english_text: Ethambutol can cause optic neuritis leading to visual disturbances; patients should report any changes in vision.
sesotho_text: Ethambutol e ka baka optic neuritis e lebisang ho mathata a pono; bakuli ba lokela ho bua ka liphetoho life kapa life tsa pono.

english_text: Common side effects of TB treatment include nausea, vomiting, and loss of appetite.
sesotho_text: Litlamorao tse tloaelehileng tsa phekolo ea TB li kenyelletsa ho nyakeloa, ho hlatsa, le ho lahleheloa ke takatso ea lijo.

english_text: Patients should take TB medication with food to reduce nausea.
sesotho_text: Bakuli ba lokela ho nka meriana ea TB le lijo ho fokotsa ho nyakeloa.

english_text: Skin rash during TB treatment may indicate a drug hypersensitivity reaction requiring medical review.
sesotho_text: Ho ruruha ha letlalo nakong ea phekolo ea TB ho ka bontša karabelo ea ho amehela haholo ke moriana e hlokang tlhahlobo ea ngaka.

english_text: Joint pain and gout can occur due to pyrazinamide-induced hyperuricaemia.
sesotho_text: Mahloko a maqhoa le gout li ka etsahala ka lebaka la hyperuricaemia e bakoang ke pyrazinamide.

english_text: Peripheral neuropathy — tingling or numbness in the hands and feet — is a side effect of isoniazid.
sesotho_text: Neuropathy ea maphethelo — ho hlohlona kapa ho fofa matsoho le maoto — ke tlhamorao ea isoniazid.

english_text: Hepatotoxicity from TB drugs presents as jaundice, dark urine, and abdominal pain.
sesotho_text: Kotsi ea sebete ho tsoa ho meriana ea TB e bontšoa e le jaundice, moroto o mootho, le mahloko a mpa.

english_text: If signs of liver toxicity appear, TB treatment should be stopped and the patient reviewed urgently.
sesotho_text: Haeba lišoaetso tsa kotsi ea sebete li hlaha, phekolo ea TB e lokela ho emisoa mme mokuloi a hlahlojoe ka potlako.

english_text: Dizziness and hearing loss can occur with aminoglycoside drugs used in drug-resistant TB treatment.
sesotho_text: Ho potoloha le ho lahleheloa ke kutlo li ka etsahala ka meriana ea aminoglycoside e sebelisoa ho phekolo ea TB e khakanyeng meriana.

english_text: Patients experiencing side effects should not stop TB treatment without consulting a healthcare provider.
sesotho_text: Bakuli ba bonang litlamorao ha ba lokela ho emisa phekolo ea TB ntle le ho buisana le mofani oa tlhokomelo ea bophelo bo botle.

english_text: Most TB treatment side effects are manageable and should not be a reason to stop treatment.
sesotho_text: Litlamorao tse ngata tsa phekolo ea TB li ka laoloa mme ha li lokela ho ba lebaka la ho emisa phekolo.

english_text: Flu-like symptoms occurring intermittently may indicate rifampicin hypersensitivity syndrome.
sesotho_text: Matšoao a tšoanang le flu a etsahalang ka nako tse fapaneng a ka bontša syndrome ea ho amehela haholo ke rifampicin.

english_text: Thrombocytopenia — low platelet count — is a rare but serious side effect of rifampicin.
sesotho_text: Thrombocytopenia — palo e tlase ea li-platelet — ke tlhamorao e sa tloaelehang empa e matla ea rifampicin.

english_text: Regular monitoring of liver function, vision, and hearing is important during TB treatment.
sesotho_text: Ho hlahlojoa ka mehla ha tšebetso ea sebete, pono, le kutlo ho bohlokoa nakong ea phekolo ea TB.

english_text: Patients should be counselled about expected side effects before starting TB treatment.
sesotho_text: Bakuli ba lokela ho fuoa keletso ka litlamorao tse nahanwang pele ho qala phekolo ea TB.

english_text: Severe or unexpected side effects during TB treatment should be reported to a clinician immediately.
sesotho_text: Litlamorao tse matla kapa tse sa nahanwang nakong ea phekolo ea TB li lokela ho buelloa ngaka hang hang.

english_text: Poor adherence to TB treatment is the main cause of treatment failure and drug resistance.
sesotho_text: Ho latela TB ho fokolang ke lebaka le leholo la ho hloleha ha phekolo le khakanyo ea meriana.

english_text: TB treatment adherence requires taking every dose of every drug for the full duration of treatment.
sesotho_text: Ho latela phekolo ea TB ho hloka ho nka dose le 'ngoe ea moriana o mong le o mong nako yohle ea phekolo.

english_text: Pill reminders, alarm clocks, and mobile phone apps can help TB patients remember their daily doses.
sesotho_text: Litemoso tsa lipilisi, li-alarm, le li-app tsa mohala li ka thusa bakuli ba TB ho hopola li-dose tsa bona tsa letsatsi le leng le le leng.

english_text: Community-based DOT allows patients to receive treatment support close to their homes.
sesotho_text: DOT e thehiloeng sechabeng e lumella bakuli ho fumana tshehetso ea phekolo haufi le malapa a bona.

english_text: Treatment supporters — family members or community volunteers — can help patients stay on track.
sesotho_text: Batshehetsi ba phekolo — maloko a lelapa kapa mahlalefi a sechaba — ba ka thusa bakuli ho lula tseleng e nepahetseng.

english_text: Social protection measures such as food vouchers and transport subsidies improve TB treatment adherence.
sesotho_text: Mehato ea tšireletso ea sechaba joalo ka li-voucher tsa lijo le lithuso tsa lipalangoa li ntlafatsa ho latela phekolo ea TB.

english_text: Addressing poverty and food insecurity is essential for improving TB treatment outcomes.
sesotho_text: Ho sebetsana le bofuma le ho hloka tšepo ea lijo ho bohlokoa ho ntlafatsa liphetho tsa phekolo ea TB.

english_text: Patients who miss doses should be contacted promptly to prevent treatment interruption.
sesotho_text: Bakuli ba lahlehetseng ke li-dose ba lokela ho ikopanyoa le bona hang hang ho thibela ho emisa phekolo.

english_text: A treatment interruption of more than two months may require restarting the full TB treatment course.
sesotho_text: Ho emisa phekolo ho feta likhoeli tse peli ho ka hloka ho qala hape khoroso yohle ea phekolo ea TB.

english_text: Motivational counselling can help patients overcome barriers to TB treatment adherence.
sesotho_text: Keletso ea khothaletso e ka thusa bakuli ho hlola meqoqo ea ho latela phekolo ea TB.

english_text: Understanding why a patient missed doses is more important than simply reminding them to take their medication.
sesotho_text: Ho utloisisa hobaneng mokuloi a lahlehetsoe ke li-dose ho bohlokoa ho feta ho mo khumamisa feela ho nka meriana ea hae.

english_text: Stigma and fear of disclosure are major barriers to TB treatment adherence.
sesotho_text: Kekello le tšabo ea ho senola ke meqoqo e meholo ea ho latela phekolo ea TB.

english_text: Employment and income loss due to TB illness can make it difficult for patients to complete treatment.
sesotho_text: Ho lahleheloa ke mosebetsi le lekeno ka lebaka la bolwetse ba TB ho ka etsa hore ho be thata bakeng sa bakuli ho phetela phekolo.

english_text: Decentralised TB treatment services reduce travel barriers and improve adherence.
sesotho_text: Litshebeletso tsa phekolo ea TB tse abeloang li fokotsa meqoqo ea ho tsamaea le ho ntlafatsa ho latela.

english_text: Digital adherence technologies such as electronic pill boxes can monitor TB treatment in real time.
sesotho_text: Liteknoloji tsa ho latela tsa dijithale joalo ka libokose tsa lipilisi tsa elektroniki li ka hlahloja phekolo ea TB nako ea nnete.

english_text: TB treatment success is defined as completing treatment without evidence of failure or relapse.
sesotho_text: Katleho ea phekolo ea TB e hlalossoa e le ho phetela phekolo ntle le bopaki ba ho hloleha kapa ho khutlela morao.

english_text: The global TB treatment success rate for drug-sensitive TB is approximately 88%.
sesotho_text: Khato ea katleho ea phekolo ea TB ea lefatše lohle bakeng sa TB e amehang ke meriana e ka bang 88%.

english_text: Treatment failure occurs when sputum cultures remain positive after five months of treatment.
sesotho_text: Ho hloleha ha phekolo ho etsahala ha li-culture tsa mathe li ntse li molemo ka mor'a likhoeli tse hlano tsa phekolo.

english_text: TB relapse occurs when a patient who completed treatment develops TB again.
sesotho_text: Ho khutlela morao ha TB ho etsahala ha mokuloi ea phetetseng phekolo a ba le TB hape.

english_text: Loss to follow-up — when a patient stops treatment without completing it — is a major challenge in TB programmes.
sesotho_text: Ho lahlehela ho latela — ha mokuloi a emisa phekolo ntle le ho e phetela — ke mathata a maholo mananeo a TB.
